title: Simultaneous equations
cover_sub: Two equations, two unknowns, one answer that fits both. Secure the method, extend it to tougher pairs, then master the quadratic cases that decide grade 8 and 9.

levels_long.s: Linear pairs: the method, step by step.
levels_long.e: Scale both equations, contexts, and one piece of tampered evidence.
levels_long.m: Quadratic pairs, unknown constants and proof.

briefing: Simultaneous equations are two equations that are both true at the same time. The solution is the pair of values, x and y, that fits both. On a graph, it's where the two lines (or the line and the curve) cross.
Elimination works for two linear equations. Substitution works when one equation already says y = …, and always when one equation is a quadratic.
method: Make the coefficients of one letter the same size. Multiply every term, including the right-hand side.
Same signs, subtract. Different signs, add. One letter disappears.
Solve for the letter that's left, then substitute back to find the other.
Check both values in the equation you didn't use. If it works, the case is closed.

example.question: A forensic unit orders kit. 3 cameras and 2 lamps cost £430. 1 camera and 2 lamps cost £210. Find the price of a camera and of a lamp.
steps: Let c = price of a camera, l = price of a lamp: 3c + 2l = 430 and c + 2l = 210
The l terms match (2l) with the same signs, so subtract: 2c = 220, so c = 110.
Substitute into the second equation: 110 + 2l = 210, so 2l = 100 and l = 50.
example.answer: A camera costs £110 and a lamp costs £50.

m.blurb: Quadratics, unknown constants and proof. Plan before you calculate.

text: A surveillance zone is the circle x² + y² = 25. A drone flies along the line y = x + 1.
Find the two points where the drone crosses the edge of the zone.
questions.tip: Expand (x + 1)² as x² + 2x + 1, not x² + 1. Then give both points, each x matched with its own y.

text: Find the coordinates of the points where the curve y = x² − 3x + 2 meets the line y = 2x − 4.
The line y = x + k touches the curve y = x² − 3x + 6 at exactly one point.
Find the value of k.
questions.working: x² − 4x + 6 − k = 0 has one root, so 16 − 4(6 − k) = 0. The line touches at (2, 4).

text: Two codes add up to 4. The sum of their squares is 58.
Find the two codes.
Show that these simultaneous equations have no solution. Explain what this means for their graphs.
questions.answer: Doubling the first gives 4x + 6y = 12, which can't also equal 15.
questions.working: Same gradient (−⅔), different intercepts: the lines are parallel and never meet.

closed_points: Solve linear pairs by elimination, scaling one or both equations first.
Use substitution when one equation is a quadratic, and give every pair of answers.
Turn a word problem into two equations with letters you define.
Spot the sign slip in someone else's working before it costs you marks.
Use the discriminant to decide when a line only touches a curve.
